nodes.summary: Call a set of natural numbers 3AP-free if it contains no $a, b, c$ with $a + c = 2b$ and $a \ne b$. There is an infinite set $A$ of natural numbers such that, for some real number $\varepsilon > 0$, every finite subset $B \subseteq A$ has a 3AP-free subset of size at least $\varepsilon |B|$, but $A$ is not the union of finitely many 3AP-free sets of natural numbers.

nodes.title: Erdős Problem 847

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of natural numbers has this property if there is a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every finite subset $B \subseteq A$ contains a subset $C \subseteq B$ with $|C| \ge \varepsilon |B|$ that contains no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression, that is, no $a, b, c \in C$ with $a + c = 2b$ and $a \ne b$.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
